questions.q: Why did Lesson 9's trigger enqueue a Queueable job rather than calling a `@future` method for the warranty claim submission?
options: Future methods cannot run asynchronously
Queueable jobs are always faster than future methods
Future methods cannot be called from Apex triggers at all
A Queueable can accept a Set<Id> (or other non-primitive state) as a constructor parameter, while future methods only accept primitive parameters
questions.explain: Future methods only accept primitive parameter types, not sObjects or collections of objects; a Queueable class can hold richer state like a Set<Id> as a member variable, which is what this design needs.

questions.q: What does `Database.QueryLocator` in `StaleInstallationJobBatch.start()` allow that a plain SOQL query in Apex does not?
options: It allows filtering on non-indexed fields only
It can address far more records than the standard SOQL row-retrieval limit, since Batch Apex processes them in chunks
It skips governor limits entirely for the whole batch job
It replaces the need for a WHERE clause
questions.explain: A QueryLocator lets Batch Apex address record sets larger than the 50,000-row SOQL retrieval limit, since the records are processed in separate chunked transactions rather than all at once.

questions.q: What is the default scope size (chunk size) Batch Apex's `execute()` method processes per transaction, per this lesson?
options: 200 records
10 records
50 records
2,000 records
questions.explain: The default scope size is 200 records per execute() call, configurable by passing a scope size to Database.executeBatch().

questions.q: What must a Queueable class implement in addition to `Queueable` to be allowed to make an HTTP callout, per this lesson?
options: Schedulable
Database.Batchable<sObject>
Database.AllowsCallouts
Comparable
questions.explain: A Queueable job must explicitly implement Database.AllowsCallouts to be permitted to make HTTP callouts -- required syntax, not optional decoration.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what shared limit applies across future methods, Queueable jobs, Batch Apex, and Scheduled Apex combined?
options: Each type has its own completely separate, unrelated daily limit
They all share one 24-hour rolling org-wide limit on total asynchronous Apex executions
Only Batch Apex has any limit; the others are unlimited
The limit only applies to orgs with fewer than 10 users
questions.explain: Future methods, Queueable, Batch, and Scheduled Apex all draw from one shared 24-hour rolling org limit on asynchronous Apex executions.
